Custom Field

Create classic custom fields for additional data tracking.

Note: This is a legacy feature. Consider using the new custom fields system instead.

Name

Enter the name of this custom field. This label appears on forms and reports.

Choose descriptive names that clearly indicate what information should be entered.

Examples: 'Purchase Order Number', 'Project Code', 'Department', 'Customer Reference'.

Position

Enter a position number to control the display order. Lower numbers appear first.

Use increments of 10 (10, 20, 30) to leave room for inserting fields later without renumbering.

Fields with the same position number are sorted alphabetically by name.

Placement

Select where this custom field should appear. You can assign it to multiple forms or line items.

Custom fields can be added to transactions, customers, suppliers, inventory items, and many other areas.

Hold Ctrl (Cmd on Mac) to select multiple placements. The field will appear on all selected forms.

Type

Select the type of custom field: Text, Paragraph text, Dropdown list, Date, Number, Amount, or Image.

Choose the type that matches your data: Text for short entries, Paragraph for longer text, Dropdown for standardized choices.

Number fields can show totals, Date fields show calendar picker, Image fields allow file uploads.

Options for drop-down list

For dropdown lists, enter the options one per line. Users will select from these predefined choices.

Dropdown lists ensure consistent data entry and make reporting easier by standardizing values.

Example: For a 'Priority' field, enter: High Medium Low

Size

Select the field size: Small, Medium, or Large. This controls the width on forms.

Small is good for codes or short values, Medium for typical text, Large for longer descriptions.

Size only affects display width - it doesn't limit the amount of text that can be entered.

Description

Enter help text that appears below the field. This guides users on what information to enter.

Good help text includes examples, format requirements, or explains why the information is needed.

Keep descriptions concise but informative. Users see this text every time they use the form.

Show custom field on printed documents

Check this box to show the custom field value on the View screen after saving.

Important custom fields should be displayed so users can quickly see key information without editing.

This is useful for reference numbers, status indicators, or other frequently viewed information.

Show at the top of printed documents

If displayed on View, check this box to show the field at the top of the View screen.

Use this for critical fields that need immediate visibility, like approval status or priority level.

Only enable for the most important fields - too many fields at the top reduces clarity.

Inactive

Check this box to deactivate this custom field. It won't appear on new forms but existing data is preserved.

Deactivate rather than delete custom fields to maintain historical data while preventing new entries.

Deactivated fields can be reactivated later if needed. Their data remains in existing records.
